clue.text: Everywhere in disarray

definitions.meaning: found in every spot, scattered far and wide

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both scattered across every location and thoroughly messy or disorganised.

clue.text: Round which it is extremely cold

definitions.text: Round which it is extremely cold

parts.words: Round which it is extremely cold
parts.note: read 'Round' as a noun: a ring of latitude near the South Pole, beyond which the climate is bitterly cold

explanation.surface: Something you might circle on a chilly day.
explanation.definitionFit: This line of latitude encircles the southern polar region, where temperatures are the lowest on Earth.

clue.text: Enjoyed having lied about 1,000

indicators.note: the word for fibbed is placed around the thousand, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: lied means told untruths
K is the usual abbreviation for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Someone happily took charge of a thousand people.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text reads 'led', but the wordplay needs 'lied': LIED placed around K gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of taking pleasure in something, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: By way of the channel bridge

parts.note: via means travelling through or by way of
a duct is a channel or pipe carrying fluid

explanation.surface: A route that takes you over the English Channel by a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' tempts you towards the English Channel, but here it is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A long elevated structure of arches carrying a road or railway across a valley is a kind of bridge.

clue.text: Came to part of the river with Edwin

parts.note: a reach is a stretch of a river between bends
Ed is a short form of the name Edwin

explanation.surface: Someone arrived at a stretch of river in Edwin's company.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrived at, as in got to a destination, the same sense as came to.

clue.text: Theo had become an impetuous person

indicators.note: the letters of the two words have turned into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Theo has turned into someone rash and quick-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts rashly and without thinking is a classic description of an impetuous person.

clue.text: One with a large bill in the chapel I canonised

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, so 'in' points to concealed letters

explanation.surface: A saintly figure with a big invoice inside the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests money owed, but it is the bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterbird is famous for its enormous beak with a throat pouch, a bill being a beak.

clue.text: Easy way to win on a race course

definitions.meaning: moving at a gentle three-beat gait, as a horse might on a racecourse

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a horse going at an easy pace and, by extension, any effortless victory.

clue.text: Came into play perhaps

parts.note: read literally: an actor stepping onstage into a drama, rather than something becoming relevant

explanation.surface: Something that became a factor in a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor arriving onstage during a drama makes an appearance in it, entering the action.

clue.text: Appear on stage maybe and pull it to pieces

definitions.meaning: play a role in a production

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to play a role in a theatrical show and to dismantle something into its components.

clue.text: Jumped on the French super train

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'
the APT was British Rail's Advanced Passenger Train, a high-speed train

explanation.surface: Someone leapt aboard a French high-speed train.
explanation.walkthrough: The APT (Advanced Passenger Train) was an experimental British high-speed train of the 1970s and 80s.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of spring or bound, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Socialist girl in Cornwall

parts.note: red is a common label for a left-winger or socialist
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A left-wing young woman living down in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county at the south-western tip of England; the definition reads as 'a place in Cornwall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Redruth is a market town in western Cornwall, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Clear in muddled terms that it's not in code

indicators.note: mixed up or confused, telling you to rearrange the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Something plain but put in confusing terms, so not encrypted.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in signalling for a message sent in plain language rather than encrypted.

clue.text: Each about right for a very long time

indicators.note: the abbreviation for each goes around the letter for right, so 'about' marks a container

parts.note: ea. is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price lists

explanation.surface: Every one of us roughly correct over an age.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch, a lengthy period of history.

clue.text: Given medical aid-free?

definitions.meaning: looked after by a doctor or nurse
paid for by someone else, so free to the recipient, as when a friend buys the drinks

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cared for medically and provided with something at another's expense.

clue.text: In a frenzy are able to work out in detail

indicators.note: wild and agitated, telling you to throw the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: Frantic people who manage to plan things thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop a plan with many intricate parts, adding detail and complexity.

clue.text: And in France one hundred — and the rest

parts.note: et is the French word for 'and'
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: In France, a hundred and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for et cetera, Latin for 'and other things', used to end a list.

clue.text: Meant not to be included in the action

indicators.note: one word is put inside another, so this phrase marks a container

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something intended not to be part of what happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meant' looks like a verb of intention, but it is used in the sense of signified; 'the' before 'action' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicated or signified, as a symbol stands for an idea.

clue.text: Before British and Foreign Off, ice leave, it means the same

indicators.note: the abbreviations depart from the first word, so 'leave' signals letters taken away

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry

explanation.surface: An instruction to quit diplomatic service, with a note on meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text splits 'Office'. Removing B and F, O from BEFORE leaves a word that means the same as 'Before'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic preposition is an exact synonym for 'before', so the result shares the starting word's sense.

clue.text: It holds wine or tea for 51 at church

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vessel at church holding wine, or tea for a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text reads '5', but the wordplay needs 51 (LI in Roman numerals).
explanation.definitionFit: The cup used for communion wine in a church service.

clue.text: Take off as I am taking one to the gallery

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
I is the Roman numeral one
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone takes a friend along to an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' here means mimic, not remove. The Tate is a group of art galleries in London and elsewhere in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, a British idiom for doing an impression.

clue.text: Make an impression in French tomb

parts.note: en is the French for 'in'
a grave is a burial place or tomb

explanation.surface: Leaving a mark inside a French burial site.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut letters or designs into a surface leaves a lasting mark in it.

clue.text: Girl had robe in crumpled condition

indicators.note: creased and disordered, telling you to jumble the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A young woman whose dress was all creased.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Lower record in clothing

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, marking a container

parts.note: dress means clothing, as in formal dress
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Putting a lower-ranked album among garments.
explanation.definitionFit: To push something down or reduce it, as when pressing a key or lowering prices.

clue.text: But interminable idler turned out to be a brickie

indicators.note: rearranged into a new form, signalling an anagram of the shortened word and the next
without end, so the first word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A lazy person who unexpectedly became a bricklayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' cuts But to BU; 'turned out' then rearranges BU with IDLER. A brickie is British slang for a bricklayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer is a construction tradesperson, one who puts up walls and houses.

clue.text: Born in endless poverty

indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym is removed, so the word has no end

parts.note: need is a state of poverty or want

explanation.surface: Someone who came into the world among the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: French for born, used before a married woman's maiden name.

clue.text: Work that is decreasing

definitions.meaning: a household chore, a job to be done
read as de-creasing: taking the creases out

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot iron is household work, and it literally removes creases.

clue.text: Thin records somehow supporting the columns

indicators.note: in some way or other, telling you to rearrange the letters

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records

explanation.surface: Flimsy albums propping up the pillars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges THIN with LPS, the abbreviation for long-playing records, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plinths are the blocks or slabs that form bases beneath columns or statues.

clue.text: Forbidden sailor also around

indicators.note: the word for 'also' goes around the sailor, marking a container

parts.note: too means also
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman, too, is banned from going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited by custom or social rule, not to be done or spoken of.

clue.text: Girl for accountant, about 50, and artist

indicators.note: the accountant abbreviation goes around fifty, marking a container

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
L is the Roman numeral fifty
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman chosen by an accountant, an artist about fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: A repair third man said was cap able of improvement

parts.note: mend means repair

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the name is replaced by a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Abel was the third man in Genesis, after Adam and his brother Cain

explanation.surface: A fix that a man described as open to being bettered.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Adam was the first man, Cain the second and Abel the third; ABEL sounds like ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be corrected or altered for the better, as a law or document may be revised.

clue.text: He was very tight at Christmas

definitions.text: He was very tight at Christmas

parts.words: He was very tight at Christmas
parts.note: tight means miserly rather than drunk: the miser of Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A man who got very drunk over the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' suggests drunk, but here it means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: The miserly hero of Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the archetypal skinflint at Yuletide.
